# Use pre-merge-review

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Gate an existing change for merge — run one skill that fires the whole production-readiness pass. First a deterministic mechanical gate (lint + typecheck + tests, via a script whose exit code decides), then the three-reviewer panel dispatched in parallel — devils-advocate (correctness), security-reviewer (exploitability), code-quality (craft) — then a single READY / NOT READY verdict. Use before opening a PR or merging, when you want the full review fleet run on a diff you already have. Do NOT use to implement a feature from a spec (that's feature-implement-loop) or to review a document (that's doc-critique).

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install pre-merge-review                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install pre-merge-review --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install pre-merge-review --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Dev team pack: [`--pack dev-team`](../packs/use-the-dev-team-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/dev-team/skills/pre-merge-review/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "is this change ready to merge?"
- "run all the reviewers on my branch before I open the PR"
- "production-readiness review of this diff"
- "gate my PR — lint, tests, and a full review"
- "review this branch and tell me if it's safe to ship"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "implement this feature from the ticket's acceptance criteria"
- "just find the bugs in this function"
- "critique this design doc"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use pre-merge-review".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The mechanical gate is run, not assumed.** A verdict with no real gate result is invalid — you ran the script (or reported `BLOCKED`), you didn't eyeball the tests.
- **The gate is un-bypassable.** A RED gate is `NOT READY` regardless of how good the review looks. The review can add blockers; it can never clear a failing gate.
- **Findings are merged and de-duped** across the three lenses — the same line is not reported three times.
- **The verdict is one word plus the blocking reasons**, not a hedged paragraph. A reader sees READY/NOT READY and exactly what stands in the way.
- **Design disagreements go to `council-review`**, not adjudicated here — this skill gates a change, it doesn't decide an architecture.

## Use something else when

- Implementing a feature from a spec — that's [`feature-implement-loop`](../../../packs/dev-team/skills/feature-implement-loop/SKILL.md), which generates and loops; this skill only judges an existing change.
- One lens is enough — a pure bug pass is [`devils-advocate`](../../../packs/dev-team/skills/devils-advocate/SKILL.md) standalone; a pure doc pass is `doc-critique`.
- An open design decision ("Postgres or Dynamo?") — that's `council-review`.

## Where a loop runs it

- Stage `verify` of the [`build` loop](../../../packs/dev-team/loops/build/LOOP.md), where gate G2 decides
